mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5% over the prior quarter reduces discount rates for future cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in a consecutive monthly series for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS tightening phase (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) accompanied by a decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate weakening labor market conditions, which typically precede equity market corrections and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% while PAYEMS falls by at least 2% in the following month
failure_condition: During the identified labor weakening regime, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 5% in a month while INDPRO falls by 2% or more
failure_condition: No significant correlation between HOUST/INDPRO divergence and SPX 5-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months suggests accelerating supply-side capacity, which typically supports equity valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO momentum persists but SPX 20-day forward returns remain negative (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the 1-month CPIAUCSL inflation rate below 2% triggers a preemptive rate cut expectation, lowering real discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative SPX 60-day returns coincide with CPIAUCSL < 2% in the 12 months following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% (UNRATE < 4%) while payrolls (PAYEMS) continue to rise, it signals a tight labor market that can drive equity risk-on flows and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE drops below 4% and PAYEMS increases by at least 1% in the following month
failure_condition: During the identified tight labor regime, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive (median ≤ 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for 10 consecutive months, it indicates persistent policy tightness that suppresses growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of FEDFUNDS > 5% for 10 consecutive months
failure_condition: During the identified high-rate period, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).
